_comment: IT IS `folio-assistant`, NOT `folio-assistant-checkout`, AND THAT IS A REVERSAL WITH A REASON. Commit e619a58c renamed this to `-checkout` to break a real collision: the root and `cat-harness/harness.json` BOTH declared `folio-assistant`, `resolveDirectories` keys `declaredBy` on the declared name, and a directory was attributable to the wrong instance while reading correctly. That fix and this branch's fix were written independently against the same defect, from opposite ends — the other side renamed the HARNESS LAYER to `cat-harness` (owner, 2026-09-20: "cat-harness, folio-assistant-core, folio-assistant are distinct instances/schemas"), which names all three and leaves `folio-assistant` free. Applying both would have been belt and braces with a cost: no instance answers to the name the owner gave, and the repository is `litlfred/folio-assistant`. So the suffix goes and the layer rename stays. The COLLISION is not what was being traded away — e619a58c's real contribution was the uniqueness test in `cat-harness/scripts/tests/check-undeclared-files.test.ts`, which is untouched, runs over the real declarations, and fails if any two share a name again. Re-adding the suffix without first re-reading that test is how this comes back. THE REPOSITORY, declared as an initialized instance. Owner, 2026-09-20: "only uploads/ on this repo's root b/c acting as if it was intialized" — this checkout is not merely the platform's source tree, it behaves as a folio that has been initialized, and an initialized instance's ingestion queue sits at ITS root. Before this, `uploads` was declared ONLY by cat-harness with instance scope, so the queue resolved to `cat-harness/uploads/` and the root had none. The obvious alternative — giving cat-harness's `uploads` entry `scope: "repository"` — was tried and MEASURED: 6 tests red, three of them the guarantee that a dependent instance inherits its own uploads/ and library/, two that the upload URL carries the instance segment. That is a real property and it is not being traded away, so the root gets its OWN declaration instead and cat-harness's is untouched.
name: folio-assistant
description: The repository itself, acting as an initialized instance. NAMED `folio-assistant-checkout` rather than `folio-assistant`, which `cat-harness/harness.json` already uses: two declarations sharing a name makes `declaredBy` and a sticky's `contributedBy` ambiguous, so a directory can be attributed to the wrong instance while reading correctly. It declares the directories a person drops things into, which belong to the checkout rather than to any one layer inside it.

directories.description: The incoming queue of the document-ingestion pipeline for THIS checkout — raw files as dropped, before ingestion. Distinct from `cat-harness/uploads/`, which is the harness layer's own queue: the two are different instances' directories that happen to share an id, not one directory declared twice. NOT L1 and NOT greppable as corpus; a source sitting here reads as absent to every consumer while the file is on disk.

_assets_comment: THE REPOSITORY'S OWN TWO FILES, declared here as of 2026-09-20 (issue #592). Before that the root instance declared NO assets at all, and `cat-harness` declared both of these with `scope: "repository"` — so the file an agent reads first was simultaneously "what this repository is" and "what the cat-harness layer is", and no instance owned it. `check:subgraph-coverage` reported nothing, because the asset DID resolve; it resolved to the wrong file's job, which is a distinction that check could not make until this split gave it two files to tell apart. The owner settled the fork on 2026-09-20: split them, so every instance owns exactly one README and one AGENTS.md, the root's being the INDEX over the others.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — folio-assistant
assets.description: The file every cold agent reads first, and the rules that bind in EVERY layer of this checkout. A layer's own AGENTS.md augments it and never restates it. `source` names the cat-bootstrap instance it descends from, so "is this still what it was copied from" is a question that can be ASKED — 'it was copied at init' is not an answer. This provenance sits here rather than on cat-harness's because THIS is the file cat-bootstrap copies at initialisation; cat-harness's own is authored in place and carries no source.

assets.title: folio-assistant
assets.description: The repository's reader-facing entry point, and the INDEX over every instance in it: its `cat-harness:instances` section is generated from the declarations themselves, giving each instance both an agent entry (AGENTS.md, memories) and a human one (README, docs). Generated sections are written by `readme:sync` only where the file already carries their markers, and `readme:audit` verifies every other link.
